name: Lake Chapala / Ajijic, Mexico

visa.notes: Temporary resident visa requires ~$1,500/mo income or ~$25,000 in savings. Renewable annually, converts to permanent after 4 years.

rent.notes: Numbeo Ajijic (Oct 2026): 3BR outside centre MXN 18,368 (~USD 980), 3BR centre MXN 26,103 (~USD 1,390); TheLatinvestor (Jul 2026) MXN 14,000-28,000 for Ajijic Centro/Riberas del Pilar/Chapala Centro, premium La Floresta MXN 35,000+. Pet-friendly 2-3BR house with yard typically USD 1,000-1,300. Converted at ~18.75 MXN/USD (Banxico FIX 18.79 on 30 Oct 2026).

healthcare.notes: IMSS Modalidad 33 voluntary enrollment for age 60-69 is MXN 20,600/yr per person from 1 Mar 2026 (~USD 92/mo, ~USD 183/mo for two); this is the min. Typical adds a basic private Mexican plan for one person (brokers quote ~USD 120-300/mo per person at 60 for Mexican-insurer plans, USD 320-500 for broader cover); max is two basic-to-mid private plans. Converted at ~18.75 MXN/USD (Banxico FIX 18.79 on 30 Oct 2026).

Converted at ~18.75 MXN/USD (Banxico FIX 18.79 on 30 Oct 2026).

healthcare.system: IMSS public system; excellent private hospitals in Guadalajara (45 min). Local clinics in Ajijic.
healthcare.waitTimes: Short at local private clinics; Guadalajara for specialists
healthcare.prescriptionCoverage: Very affordable; many meds available over the counter

pros: Largest US/Canadian expat community in Mexico
Spring-like climate year-round at lake elevation
